look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Is this a rhizomatous upright herb, rather than a large woody sagebrush shrub? Check the soft silvery or two-toned stem leaves (entire, toothed or lobed), then the many small, inconspicuous flower heads in a narrow to branched cluster. Leaf color alone cannot confirm the species.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts Artemisia ludoviciana at species rank and recognizes multiple subspecies. Approved Master Plant Pool source is species-level; do not force a subspecies from the selected Idaho photograph. Distinct from woody Artemisia tridentata.

morphology_keys.habit: Aromatic, spreading rhizomatous perennial herb, typically 20–80 cm tall; stems erect, simple or branched, often hairy.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Leaves along stems, linear to broadly elliptic, about 1.5–11 cm long; margins entire, toothed or variably lobed; gray-green, white-silvery or two-toned with hairs. Variation includes subspecies.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Small disciform heads grouped in compact or open branched arrays, erect to nodding; involucres approximately 2–4 mm with densely woolly gray-green phyllaries; ray florets absent.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Tiny dry one-seeded cypselae, around 0.5 mm; no conspicuous pappus.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Look for herbaceous upright stems and spreading rhizomes; do not identify solely from gray foliage.

confused_with: Artemisia tridentata (persistent three-tipped wedge-shaped leaves on a woody shrub, not a rhizomatous herb)
Artemisia vulgaris (often strongly two-toned leaves, more deeply cut and often taller; examine several leaves and heads)
Artemisia douglasiana (broader often entire leaves, generally taller; western comparison)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Combine perennial rhizomatous herb habit, variable silver or bicolored cauline leaves, and small woolly-involucred heads. Big sagebrush is a much woodier shrub with persistent small wedge-shaped leaves usually shallowly three-tipped.
